title: Integrative extraction of primary metabolites and proteins from Deinococcus radiodurans
author: Emanuel Ott

1. Centrifuge at 3000 g / 4 °C / 3 min (in Falcon tubes) 2. Discard supernatant and dissolve pellet in 1.8 mL cold PBS (transfer to homogenization tube) 3. Centrifuge at 1500 g / 4 °C / 3 min 4. Repeat step 2 and 3 two times 5. Discard washing solution and resuspend pellet in 1 mL cold, freshly prepared MCW (methanol 2.5 : chloroform 1 : water 0.5) 6. Homogenize in bead beater (e.g. Roche MagNA Lyser 4x 7000 rpm, 30 sec; chill between cycles) 7. Agitate for 10 sec, incubate 15 min on ice (shake once a while) 8. Centrifuge 21000 g / 4 °C / 5 min 9. Separate supernatant (contains metabolites) from pellet (contains proteins and nucleic acids)

1. Resuspend Pellet in Trizol 2. Homogenize one more time in the bead beater to dissolve pellet completely (Roche MagNA Lyser 1x 7000 rpm, 30 sec) 3. Incubate on a turning wheel at RT / 5 min 4. Add 200 µL Chloroform and shake vigorously for 15 sec 5. Incubate on a turning wheel at RT / 2-3 min 6. Centrifuge at 12000 rpm / 4 °C / 15 min 7. Remove aquaous phase (contains nucleic acids) 8. Add 400 µL water and incubate on turning wheel at RT / 2-3 min 9. Centrifuge at 12000 rpm / 4 °C / 15 min and remove aquaous phase 10. Precipitate the proteins by adding 5x 100 mM ammonium acetate in MeOH 11. Incubate overnight at -20 °C

1. Acclimate sample at room temperature when using frozen samples to avoid condensation 2. Redissolve sample in methoximation reagent (40mg Methoxyaminhydrochlorid (CH 3 ONH 2 *HCL) in 1ml Pyridine) for methoximation 3. Incubate 90 min. at 30°C using a thermo shaker 4. Add 80 µL MSTFA (N-Methyl-N-(trimethylsilyl) trifluoroacetamide) for silylation 5. Incubate for 30 min at 37 °C 6. Centrifuge at 14000 g / 2 min 7. 1. Chop the gel pieces with a scalpel over a glass plate. The final size of acrylamide pieces should be around 1 mm 3 . Glass plate should be carefully cleaned after each gel piece. Avoid taking gel without proteins.2. Transfer the gel pieces to a 1.5 mL LoBind tube and keep them on mQH 2 O until all samples are processed.3. Remove water and add 1 mL of 25 mM AmBic, incubate 15 min at 37 °C in a thermal shaker. Discard supernatant.4. Add 1 mL of 25 mM AmBic, 50% ACN, incubate 15 min at 37 °C in a thermal shaker. Discard supernatant. Repeat ( The supernatant must be almost transparent or with a very light blue colour, if the blue colour is intense, repeat again. Band destaining and cleaning is crucial for a good LC-MS analysis. In these steps not only coomassie, but also SDS and other contaminants are removed. If there is still blue colour inside the gel pieces after three washing steps, continue with the protocol, it will not interfere with protein digestion. This usually happens when the gel pieces are not small enough.) 5. Dehydrate gel pieces with 300 μL 100% ACN incubate 5 min at RT in a shaker. Discard supernatant. ( At this point gel pieces should be much reduced in volume, hard, and completely white, having a “plastic” look. If they are still translucent or soft repeat this step (you can use the pipette tip to test it).) 6. Reduce disulphide bonds with 20 mM DTT in 100 mM AmBic (cover gel pieces) at 37 °C for 30 min.7. Add 500 µL of 100% ACN to shrink gel pieces to remove DTT.8. Alkylate reduced Cys residues by adding 55 mM IAA in 100 mM AmBic (cover gel pieces) at RT in DARK for 60min.9. Remove all IAA solution10. Wash with 500 µL 25 mM AmBic, incubate 15 min at 37 °C in a thermal shaker. Discard supernatant.11. Wash with 25 mM AmBic, 50% ACN, incubate 15 min at 37 °C in a thermal shaker. Discard supernatant.12. Dehydrate gel pieces with 300 μL 100% ACN incubate 5 min at RT in a shaker. Discard supernatant. 13. Dry out in a SpeedVac for 5 min.14. Add 50 μL of Trypsin Solution to each tube and incubate 15 minutes at 37 °C. If needed, add more trypsin solution until the gel pieces are completely rehydrated. Wait another 15 minutes. Completely cover the gel pieces with trypsin buffer.[Trypsin Solution: dilute Trypsin Sequencing Grade (Roche 11 418 475 001) to 10-12.5 ng/μL. Add 1 mL of trypsin buffer to the vial, incubate on ice for 10 min and then pipet up and down to completely resuspend the pellet. Transfer to a 2 mL LoBind tube. Add 1 mL of trypsin buffer to the vial, washing all the walls. Then transfer to the previous tube. Trypsin can be stored at -20 °C for 1 month. It is recommended to make aliquots to avoid melt/freezing cycles that can damage the enzyme. Aliquots should be stored in low binding tubes.];[ Trypsin Buffer : 25 mM NH 4 HCO 3 (AmBic), 10% (v/v) acetonitrile, 5 mM CaCl 2 . Calcium must be added in last place to avoid precipitation. Prepare fresh.]15. Incubate 14-16 h at 37 °C. Incubation in an oven is recommended, if a thermal block is used, cover it with aluminium foil to maintain the temperature also in the caps of the tubes. No shaking!

steps.title: Grow D. radiodurans culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate Deinococcus radiodurans in a suitable medium (e.g., TGB or TGY) and grow to obtain sufficient biomass for the experiment. TGB recipe: 1 % tryptone, 0.6 % beef extract, 0.2 % glucose.

steps.title: Metabolite phase separation and drying
steps.instruction: Perform liquid‑liquid extraction of metabolites from the cell‑free supernatant, then dry the polar phase in a speed‑vacuum using a defined pressure gradient and store.

substeps.instruction: Add 400 µL water to the supernatant to induce phase separation.
Agitate briefly and centrifuge at 14 000 g for 2 min.
Transfer the upper (polar) phase to a new Eppendorf tube; the lower apolar phase may be stored separately if desired.
Dry the polar extracts in a speed‑vacuum with the following gradient: 200 mbar 30 min → 120 mbar 30 min → 80 mbar 30 min → 50 mbar 30 min → 20 mbar 30 min → 0.001 mbar for 3–4 h.
Store the dried metabolite samples overnight at –20 °C.

steps.title: Wash protein pellet with acetone
steps.instruction: Clean the protein pellet obtained after metabolite extraction by repeated acetone washes and air‑drying.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the sample at 5 000 g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant by pipetting.
Add 1 mL acetone to the pellet, pipette up/down or place in a soft ultrasound bath to disaggregate.
Centrifuge at 5 000 g for 5 min at 4 °C and discard the supernatant.
Repeat the acetone wash two additional times (total of three washes).
Air‑dry the pellet until all acetone has evaporated.
Store the dried pellet at –20 °C overnight.

steps.title: Solubilize proteins and BCA assay
steps.instruction: Resuspend the protein pellet in urea/SDS buffer, clarify, and determine protein concentration using a BCA assay compatible with SDS.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 8 M urea, 4 % (w/v) SDS. Start with 20–30 µL buffer; add more if the solution becomes highly viscous or proteins remain undissolved.
Incubate up to 3 h in a thermal shaker at 35 °C, 750 rpm, with occasional pipetting to aid solubilisation.
Centrifuge the lysate at 21 000 g for 5 min to remove insoluble debris.
Prepare Standard Working Reagent (SWR) by mixing 100 vol reagent A with 2 vol reagent B (stable 1 week at RT).
Reagent A (100 mL): 0.1 g sodium bicinchoninate, 2.0 g Na₂CO₃·H₂O, 0.16 g sodium tartrate·2H₂O, 0.4 g NaOH, 0.95 g NaHCO₃; adjust pH to 11.25 with NaHCO₃ or NaOH if needed.
Reagent B (10 mL): 0.4 g CuSO₄·5H₂O dissolved in water. Reagents A and B are stable indefinitely at RT.
Prepare BSA standards (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 15, 20 µg) in the same urea/SDS buffer as the samples; run each in three technical triplicates.
Add 2 µL of each sample or standard to wells of an ELISA plate.
Add 200 µL SWR to each well, shake gently, and seal the plate with a cap or aluminium foil.
Incubate 20 min at 60 °C (or 40 min at 45 °C in a plate reader).
Measure absorbance at 562 nm. Note: BCA is compatible with SDS but not with reducing agents such as DTT or β‑mercaptoethanol.

steps.title: Prepare and run SDS-PAGE
steps.instruction: Cast resolving and stacking gels, load protein samples, and perform electrophoresis under defined voltage conditions.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 10× running buffer (TGS): dissolve 10 g SDS, 30.2 g Tris‑Base, 144 g glycine in water and bring volume to 1 L.
Prepare resolving gel solution (12.5 % acrylamide:bisacrylamide, 0.1 % SDS, 0.375 M Tris‑HCl pH 8.8, 0.2 % TEMED, 0.073 % APS).
Cast the resolving gel, quickly overlay with 2‑propanol to avoid bubbles, and polymerise for 1 h.
Prepare stacking gel solution (5 % acrylamide:bisacrylamide, 0.2 % SDS, 0.225 M Tris‑HCl pH 6.8, 0.2 % TEMED, 0.1 % APS).
Before adding TEMED and APS, discard the 2‑propanol layer covering the resolving gel and rinse briefly with water.
Pour the stacking solution, insert the comb carefully avoiding bubbles.
Take 40–80 µg of each protein sample, add 2 µL 5× Laemmli buffer (80 % glycerol, 20 % SDS, 20 % β‑mercaptoethanol, 0.01 % bromophenol blue), and bring volume to 10 µL with water.
Load samples into wells, leaving a blank well between each to prevent cross‑contamination.
Run the gel at constant 40 V until the dye front reaches the stacking‑resolving interface.
Increase voltage to constant 80 V and run until bromophenol blue migrates ~1 cm into the stacking gel.
Stop electrophoresis.

steps.title: Stain, destain, and cut gel
steps.instruction: Coomassie‑stain the gel, destain, wash, and excise lanes for downstream peptide work.

substeps.instruction: Immediately transfer the gel to Coomassie staining solution (40 % MeOH, 10 % acetic acid, 0.1 % Coomassie R‑250 in water) and incubate 30 min with shaking.
Destain the gel in 40 % MeOH, 2 % acetic acid in water, replacing the destain solution every 20 min for a total of 80 min.
Wash the gel in distilled water for 30 min.
Cut the lanes out of the gel; cover with water before freezing if long‑term storage is required.
Store gel pieces at –20 °C (or –80 °C for extended storage).

steps.title: Extract peptides from gel pieces
steps.instruction: Recover tryptic peptides from the excised gel fragments using sequential organic extractions and speed‑vac drying.

substeps.instruction: Add 150 µL of 50 % acetonitrile (ACN), 1 % formic acid (FA) to each tube containing gel pieces; incubate 5 min at room temperature.
Sonicate the tubes in a low‑intensity ultrasound bath for 3 min.
Centrifuge at 21 000 g for 1 min and transfer the supernatant to the same tube.
Add 100 µL of 90 % ACN, 1 % FA, incubate 5 min at room temperature, and transfer this supernatant to the same tube.
Dry the combined extracts in a SpeedVac using the same pressure gradient as in step 2 (metabolite drying).
Store the dried peptide extracts at –20 °C or proceed directly to desalting; for long‑term storage keep at –80 °C.

steps.title: Resuspend peptide pellets
steps.instruction: Dissolve dried peptide pellets in solubilisation buffer and ensure complete recovery before desalting.

substeps.instruction: Add 75 µL peptide solubilisation (PS) buffer (4 % ACN, 0.25 % FA) to each pellet.
Incubate 10 min on ice.
Resuspend by pipetting and sonicate in a low‑intensity ultrasound bath for 3 min.
Incubate 5 min at room temperature, then keep the solution on ice.

steps.title: Desalt peptides using C18 tips
steps.instruction: Purify the peptide solution on C18 stage‑tips (or 96‑well plates) through activation, equilibration, binding, washing, and elution steps.

substeps.instruction: Activate each C18 tip by passing 400 µL MeOH through twice; allow flow to waste by gravity for 3 min each time, then aspirate.
Equilibrate the tip by passing 400 µL Milli‑Q water four times; allow flow to waste for 3 min each, then aspirate.
Load the entire peptide solution (including any insoluble material) onto the tip; let it flow by gravity for 10 min, then aspirate. Confirm that the membrane has retained the peptides.
Wash the bound peptides with 400 µL Milli‑Q water five times (avoid excessive vacuum pressure).
Aspirate to near dryness (~1 min).
Elute peptides by passing 200 µL MeOH through the tip twice; allow flow by gravity for >5 min each, then aspirate.
Apply vacuum if needed to ensure complete elution.
Transfer the eluate to LoBind tubes and dry in a SpeedVac.
The desalted peptides are now ready for LC‑MS analysis.
